Remark
[Riemann invariants for $m>2$] ↗ def:riemann-invariant 1. ch11:11.3-rem-1\group Conservation Laws

For $m>2$, Riemann invariants need not exist.

Assume \[ (4)\qquad \mathbf w(z)=(w^1(z),w^2(z)) \] is a local coordinate map with inverse $\mathbf z(w)$, let $\mathbf u$ be a smooth solution of (1), and set \[ (5)\qquad \mathbf v(x,t)=\mathbf w(\mathbf u(x,t)). \]
